title: Bayesilisk Core Access-Control Motifs (category-theory motifs)
framing: Category-theory motifs: ABAG tokens are objects, connector actions are morphisms (requires -> produces), workflow-sequence motifs are composite morphisms, and a connector is a functor F:A->App that executes abstract tokens via their concrete `refines`. Motifs are typed diagram obligations checked deterministically.
provenance: Curated by the Bayesilisk maintainers from common authorization and data-boundary failure classes. Several motifs are validated against the worked Cal.com connector example (examples/calcom), including findings with upstream human-authored fixes.
references: examples/calcom (worked real-app connector with upstream-validated findings)

motifs.rationale: An identifier that does not resolve to any object must return not-found, not silently expose or fabricate state, even when the identifier is an optional reference that otherwise degrades into a default flow.
motifs.validatedBy: examples/calcom: unknown/stale rescheduleUid opened the booking flow (HTTP 200) instead of 404; upstream fix PR calcom/cal.com#29400 (approved).

motifs.rationale: A principal must not read or act on an object owned by another principal by swapping its identifier.
A principal must not reach a resource scoped to another tenant by swapping a tenant-scoped identifier.
An identifier for a deleted or expired object must not resolve as if the object were still live.
An expired credential or session token must be rejected, never accepted as still valid.
A single-use token replayed after consumption must be rejected to prevent action replay.
A client-supplied value for a server-controlled property must not be honored (mass assignment).
An identifier that is valid but belongs to a different parent/context resource must be rejected, not silently resolved against the requested context.
motifs.validatedBy: examples/calcom: a rescheduleUid for another event type was accepted on the wrong event-type route (expected 409).

mutation.title: identifier from a different parent context

motifs.rationale: An identifier for a cancelled resource replayed against an action route must be rejected, distinct from a deleted/expired identifier.
motifs.validatedBy: examples/calcom: cancelled booking direct reschedule route is expected to return 409.

motifs.rationale: A reset/single-use token that has been superseded by a newer one must remain invalid afterwards.
motifs.validatedBy: examples/calcom: a superseded password-reset token is expected to remain invalid (410).

motifs.rationale: An action on a sub-resource must require a concrete authorized reference; a missing or guessed sub-resource reference must not authorize the action.
motifs.validatedBy: examples/calcom: a random/missing seat reference must not expose seated-booking cancellation (403).

motifs.rationale: Replaying a public identifier of a cancelled resource across a boundary must be rejected.
motifs.validatedBy: examples/calcom: create-booking -> cancel-booking -> open-public-booking-route(rescheduleUid=booking.uid) returned 200 instead of 409 (calcom/cal.com issue #29407).
pattern: replay old public identifier across boundary

motifs.rationale: After a privilege is revoked or a session is downgraded, a stale privileged session must not still act.
An invitation token that was revoked must not be acceptable afterwards.
